A11.name: Labeled
A11.note: Every example has a known target.

A13.name: Weakly labeled
A13.note: Targets exist but are noisy, partial, or generated by a heuristic rather than verified by hand.

A14.name: Semi-supervised
A14.note: A small labeled portion sits inside a much larger unlabeled pool, and both are used together.

A15.name: Self-labeled
A15.note: Labels manufactured from the data itself (a pretext task).

A22.name: Sequential
A22.note: Order matters; position depends on what came before.

A23.name: Spatial
A23.note: Neighboring values in 2D/3D space are related.

A24.name: Graph-structured
A24.note: Rows connect through explicit edges to other rows.

A25.name: Hierarchical
A25.note: Nested containment: points belong inside other points.

A26.name: Set-structured
A26.note: A collection of elements with membership but no order.

A33.name: Ordinal
A33.note: Discrete categories with a meaningful order.

A34.name: Text
A34.note: Free-form natural language, read as sequences of tokens.

A35.name: Image
A35.note: Pixel grids, where spatial arrangement itself carries signal.

A37.name: Graph-native
A37.note: Each example is itself a graph object.

A38.name: Mixed
A38.note: More than one modality in one table.

A42.name: High-dimensional
A42.note: Many features, possibly more than samples.

A43.name: Sparse
A43.note: Most values are zero or missing.

A53.name: Stationary
A53.note: Statistical properties don't move over time.

A54.name: Non-stationary
A54.note: Distribution shifts over time. This is drift.

A55.name: Linearly separable
A55.note: Classes can be split by a straight line/plane.

A62.name: Missing at random
A62.note: Gaps unrelated to the value itself.

A63.name: Missing not at random
A63.note: Gaps depend on the missing value itself.

A64.name: Noisy
A64.note: Values present but corrupted or imprecise.
